newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - June 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - June 26.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

New Zealand businessman Graeme Hart has refused to confirm if he is planning a take-over bid for major Australian food product company Burns Philp. Earlier this month Hart's Rank Group Pty Ltd company bought a 14.74 per cent holding in the company and in trading last night it increased that stake. Page 21.

Imperial Chemicals Industries plc has announced it is severed several agreements with ICI Australia after selling its 62.4 per cent shareholding in the company. The move will force ICI Australia to increase its expenditure on research and development, and will cost the company about A$150 million in lost annual revenue. Page 21.

Prominent Australian gold industry figure Joseph Gutnick has forecast a revival in the gold bullion price and criticised market analysts for their lack of support for local companies. Speaking at an Australia-Israel Chamber of Commerce lunch, Gutnick cited comments by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, who says Japan is considering dropping US Treasury bonds and investing in gold instead, in support of his predictions. Page 22.

The Victorian Government has awarded a contract to own and operate five new nursing homes to Moran Healthcare. This is the first instance of privatisation of the nursing care market in Victoria, and advances Moran Healthcare to market leader among the Sttes private nursing home operators. Page 23.

Australian manufacturing and engineering company Hawker Richardson Ltd has rejected the A$58 million take-over bid from Alan Jackson. Managing director Graeme Salthouse said yesterday that as the company had recently expanded at a rate that had doubled market capitalisation within the past year and investors should not sell at this time. Page 23.

Following their recent alignment, the Patrick stevedoring business has assumed sole operational control of Lang Corp. Patrick's chief executive Chris Corrigan said yesterday the management restructuring would allow for improved productivity at Lang Corp nd vowed to follow the future directions mapped out by the previous leaders. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian Securities Commission is conducting preliminary inquiries into trading in newspaper group John Fairfax Holdings by its major shareholder Brierley Investments BIL, Merrill Lynch and Westpac Banking Corp. Only Westpac spokeswoman Glenda Hewtt was available for comment yesterday, saying the bank would co-operate fully with the ASC in its investigations. Page 23.

BHP is expected to reduce the value of its A$2.3 billion Magma Copper interests by up to A$500 million. BHP directors are expected to confirm the decision today when they hold committee meetings to review their asset writedowns and to determine the compay's profit announcement for the year ending May 30, due this Friday. Page 23.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has announced the rates telecommunications companies will pay in order to gain access to the Telstra network following full deregulation on July 1. The interim rates will reduce interconnection fees by aout 35 per cent and will apply until the results of negotiations between Telstra and service providers for permanent rates that will apply from January 1 1998 are announced. Page 25.

Telecommunications company Northgate Communications Australia is confident about its future following full deregulation of the industry on July 1. Northgate set up operations in March this year establishing a pay-TV and telephony service in Ballarat, Vicoria as part of its long-term plan to lay a A$20 million broadband cable network across the State. Page 25.

A study by RGS Communications of the smartcard market titled Loyalty Languish has found that consumers have little brand loyalty and that less than 17 per cent of the large number of users of the programs access the rewards offered. One example provided as how only two per cent of people who held Fly Buys cards claimed their free flight entitlements. Page 26.

A survey of 615 company directors on tariff issues, released yesterday by the Australian Institute of Company Directors and accounting firm KPMG, has found that approximately half of them believe the Australian economy has suffered from globalisation and hat tariff reductions should be suspended until other nations make cuts in their protection levels. The survey also found that 73 per cent of directors did not believe APEC assurances of free trade being established in developing countries. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Tax Commissioner Michael Carmody cautioned taxpayers yesterday over how they often failed to include taxable allowances, such as site allowances and bank account interest, on their tax returns. Other mistakes Carmody highlighted included the claiming of deductions for the cost of trips between work and home and for clothing and footwear worn daily at work. Page 29.

A consortium led by the Macquarie Bank is expected to buy the Federal Government's automotive fleet management company DASfleet for approximately A$400 million. Federal Finance Minister John Fahey and the Office of Asset Sales have been wn over by the aggressiveness of the bid by the investment bank, with an announcement confirming the win likely next week. Page 29.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has called on capital markets to act on the Government's reforms to the Income Tax Assessment Act which would make it easier for lenders to borrow overseas. Costello claimed the amendments would help to reduce interest raes for small business and home borrowers. Page 20.

The ABC Board yesterday approved further discussions with three groups believed to be interested in purchasing the Asian satellite television service, Australia Television. The three groups are Steve Vizard's Artists Services, Kerry Packer's Publishing ad Broadcasting and Kerry Stokes. Page 31.

The A$400 million butter and margarine market is to face increased competition following the launch of a A$2 million advertising campaign promoting a new product with the slogan "I can't believe it's not Butter", aimed at people who enjoy butter's taste but are aware of its health drawbacks. The product is produced by Unilever owned FLORAfoods and will be launched on Sunday. Page 32.

Advertising will be allowed on pay-TV from July 1 as part of the full deregulation in the telecommunications industry. The commercials will not follow the traditional 30 second format, but will instead take at more sophisticated approach aimed at attractng target audience groups. Page 32.
THE AGE

Leading Australian gold company Newcrest Mining Ltd announced yesterday it was dropping expansion plans for its main operation, the Telfer mine in Western Australia, and downgrading the value of the project by A$100 million. Managing director Ian Johnson said the move would ensure funding for its planned gold exploration project at Cadia in New South Wales. Page B1.

ICI Australia shareholders yesterday strongly supported the company's decision to reduce the shareholder base by buying back and cancelling up to A$360 million company shares. Company investors voted in a formal ballot at a extraordinary general meeting in Melbourne yesterday. Page B1.

Shareholders of Bank of Western Australia yesterday gave the go-ahead to an employment share incentive plan and executive option scheme. The decision was taken at the first annual meeting held in Perth for the newly listed company, and shareholders were warned by chairman Ian Mackenzie that the bank would find it difficult this financial year to match last year's net profit. Page B2.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission yesterday approved the purchase by New Zealand-based Fletcher Challenge of the remaining 50 per cent of Australian Newsprint Mills from News Ltd for A$250 million. Commission chairman Allan Fels said appoval had been granted on the basis that the move increases global competition. Page B3.

Changes introduced in the last two years by Goodman Fielder managing director David Hearn have earned the approval of the market with shares in the company yesterday reaching a six-year high. Reforms have included the sale of non profitable assets and acquisitions including the purchase of New Zealand company Defiance Mills' DFM.AX baking operations. Page B2.

Industry analysts are undecided about the viability of the merger of Australian nickel company QNI with South African mining giant Gencor. If it succeeds, the A$2.3 billion merger will create a major new force on the world nickel market, but Australian market support for the take-over has so far been only lukewarm, with investors having doubts on the profitability of Gencor's nickel mines world-wide. Page B2.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
